title: Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956 — Section 18
act: The Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956

legal_context.subject: Maintenance of a Hindu wife
legal_context.important_note: Section 18 concerns the entitlement of a Hindu wife to maintenance from her husband and circumstances in which she may live separately without forfeiting her claim.

section_18.title: Maintenance of wife

statutory_text.subsection_1: Subject to the provisions of this section, a Hindu wife, whether married before or after the commencement of this Act, shall be entitled to be maintained by her husband during her lifetime.

subsection_2.intro: A Hindu wife shall be entitled to live separately from her husband without forfeiting her claim to maintenance if:

grounds.a: He is guilty of desertion, that is to say, of abandoning her without reasonable cause and without her consent or against her wish, or of wilfully neglecting her.
grounds.b: He has treated her with such cruelty as to cause a reasonable apprehension in her mind that it will be harmful or injurious to live with her husband.
grounds.d: He has any other wife living.
grounds.e: He keeps a concubine in the same house in which his wife is living or habitually resides with a concubine elsewhere.
grounds.f: He has ceased to be a Hindu by conversion to another religion.
grounds.g: There is any other cause justifying her living separately.

statutory_text.subsection_3: A Hindu wife shall not be entitled to separate residence and maintenance from her husband if she is unchaste or ceases to be a Hindu by conversion to another religion.

section_18.plain_summary: Section 18 provides that, subject to the section's conditions, a Hindu wife is entitled to maintenance from her husband during her lifetime. It also recognizes specified circumstances in which she may live separately without losing her maintenance claim.
key_elements: The provision applies to a Hindu wife.
The wife is entitled to be maintained by her husband during her lifetime, subject to the section.
A wife may live separately without forfeiting her maintenance claim in specified circumstances.
Cruelty creating a reasonable apprehension that living with the husband would be harmful or injurious is one recognized ground.
Having another wife living is one recognized ground.
Keeping a concubine in the same house or habitually residing with a concubine elsewhere is one recognized ground.
Conversion of the husband to another religion is one recognized ground.
Any other cause justifying separate residence is one recognized ground.
Sub-section (3) specifies circumstances in which the wife is not entitled to separate residence and maintenance under this section.
rag_use: Identify Section 18 as a possible maintenance route when the facts indicate that the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act may apply.
Ask relevant questions about the marital relationship and circumstances of separate residence.
Distinguish statutory eligibility questions from the amount of maintenance.
Do not automatically conclude that a user is entitled to maintenance solely from one stated fact.
Flag fact-specific eligibility questions for appropriate human or legal review.

application_to_alimony_plus.calculator_rule: Section 18 does not provide a fixed mathematical formula for calculating maintenance. Do not infer a guaranteed amount from this section.
application_to_alimony_plus.safety_rule: The AI should explain the statutory provision and its stated grounds without deciding legal entitlement.
application_to_alimony_plus.human_review: Fact-specific questions concerning eligibility, separate residence, conduct, conflicting proceedings, or interpretation of the statutory grounds should be escalated for appropriate legal or human review.
